This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of one Govindaraja in a motor vehicles accident dated 15.01.2019.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Petitioners are the parents of deceased- Gondaraja.
It is the case of the petitioners' that on 15.01.2019 at 5:00 hours, deceased was driving a car bearing Reg.No.KA-29-N-4279 from Solapur side towards Ahmadnagar.

At that time a Trailer bearing Reg.No.RJ-17-GD-9341(hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle' for short) being driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came from the opposite side and dashed against the car.
In the said accident, deceased sustained injuries and died on the spot.
3.1 At the time of accident, deceased was 30 years, earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Petitioners being the parents of deceased were dependent on him.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have appeared and filed separate written statement denying that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
They have disputed the age, occupation, income of the deceased and also that petitioners were dependents on him.
5. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
6. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner No.2 is examined as PW.1 and one witness as PW.2.

They have relied upon Exs.P1 to 9.
7.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any oral evidence.
Ex. R1
is marked on their behalf.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.18,26,300/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed Hanamantgouda S/O Timmanagouda Bandi ... vs Jitendra S/O Ladhu Ram Bishnol And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187897544/
2 respondent No.2 to pay the same.

The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded  1. Loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/-
petitioner

No.1  2. Loss of filial consortium of Rs.40,000/-
 petitioner No.2  3. Funeral, obsequies ceremony Rs.15,000/-
 and conveyance  4.

For loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 5. For loss of dependency Rs.17,13,600/-

During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2019, the income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side and it requires reconsideration.
10. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

11. Heard arguments and perused the records.
12.
Though the petitioners are pleaded that deceased was aged 30 years based on the transfer certificate the Tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 27 years and consequently multiplier 17.
The Tribunal has correctly added 40% towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma Insurance Company case).

sentences.text: In the absence of proof that deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month the Tribunal has taken his income as Rs.12,000/- on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2019, based on minimum wages the income ought to have been taken at Rs.13,250/-.
40% of it comes to Rs.5,300/-.
Therefore, the income is required to taken at Rs.18,550/-.
Since deceased was bachelor, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% towards his personal and living expenses.

With t h e s e c o m p o n e n t s t h e c o m p e n s a t i o n u n d e r t h e h e a d l o s s o f d e p e n d e n c y i s Rs.18,550x12x17x50%=Rs.18,92,100/- as against Rs.17,13,600/- granted by the Tribunal.

13. Based on the decision of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and (2018) 18 SCC 130 others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma Insurance Company case, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation of dead body) the same requires no interference.

To this extent the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.

ii. Appellants/petitioners are entitled for  compensation in a sum of Rs.20,02,100/- together with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.18,23,600/-
granted by the Tribunal.

iii. Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6%
p.a. (Minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
iv.
Vide order dated 12.01.2023, the petitioners are not entitled to interest for delay of 72 days on the enhanced compensation.
v. Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
